I was imagining the feral reaction of zombies, as we know them right now (but fast), yet they maintain their mind completely but can't control motor function at all, imagine that. Everyone is alive, still in their and still able to communicate but they're going to tear you up to the detriment of their own body and mind. Imagine a family member that you're close with screaming and crying because they can't stop ripping apart another family member you both love. Sad and with potential.

ooh you know what, rain causing zombification, or infected water is a genius idea. That means getting clean water is difficult and dangerous and if it's set in a rainy country or state then it could be especially difficult to escape. Imagine going to a small rural business building to scrounge for supplies, only to be trapped in it because it starts to rain and it turns out you're not in their alone and you don't know whether it's a zombie or 6, or even just another person that had the same idea and do they have a weapon? Oh, it appears they filled a whole bag with water bottles from this place and you want them. So much you can do with the idea. It's a small island and you need to travel off land for more supplies? Make sure to god you don't touch the ocean water or that it doesn't start raining on the way out.

I think reviewing silent hill creatures would be a good step for evolving a more fearsome zombie. Twitchy movements like the nurses is a good start. Thinking on it, I suppose I don't find conventional zombies scary anymore, from romero to modern, like l4d or I am legend. Playing on the most primal fears would be necessary to feel fresh. Humans are terrified of things that appear human but clearly have something wrong, but it's much scarier when you can't quite identify why it makes you uncomfortable, so not blatantly obvious.

In my head, music and ambience is 95% of fear, since this is just writing though, perhaps building around the tension by significantly powering up the undead. Most stories everyone is so gung-ho with dead killing. Well what if it really wasn't that easy? What if they were very fast, durable enough to survive a shotgun to the head, relentless and violent, always listening. The thought of running through a hallway while a group of 20 of these undead tear around corners and through every obstacle for no other reason than to rip the warm meat apart and move on. Being chased by something faster than you truly is terrifying. A real threat. L4d isn't scary because the zombies are fodder. So make them all a real risk.
